title: Stacks lemma for a reduced closed subcurve of a nodal curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $X$ be a reduced finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Suppose that at every closed point $x$ where $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is not smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is finite separable over $k$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and its completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is, as a $k$-algebra, $\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(uv)$ (maximal-ideal-adic completion and two-variable formal power series [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]). If $Y\subset X$ is a reduced closed subscheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] equidimensional of dimension $1$, then (1) at every nonsmooth closed point $y$ of $Y$ its residue field is finite separable over $k$ and its completed local ring is $\kappa(y)[[u,v]]/(uv)$; and (2) if $Z\subset X$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus Y$ (the smallest closed subscheme through which the open immersion factors), then (a) the scheme-theoretic intersection $Y\cap Z$ is a finite disjoint union of spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] of finite separable extensions of $k$, (b) every point of $Y\cap Z$ is a nonsmooth node of $X$ with completed local ring $\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(uv)$, and (c) $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth at every point of $Y\cap Z$.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), parts (1) and (2)(a)--(c), specialized to split nodes; finite type makes the discrete boundary finite. The explicit completed-local-ring convention is the split case of Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal) and Remark 0CBU (remark-trivial-quadratic-extension).

proof.text: A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-trf-complementary-pure-subcurve-components] to $Y\subseteq X$: $Y$ is the reduced union of a subset of the finitely many irreducible components, and the reduced closure of $X\setminus Y$ is the union of the remaining components. The open $X\setminus Y$ is reduced (its stalks are stalks of $X$), so [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image] identifies that reduced closure with the scheme-theoretic closure $Z$ in the statement. Put $T=Y\cap Z$. No generic point of an irreducible component of $X$ lies in both unions. Any nonclosed point of a Noetherian scheme of dimension one is generic in a component: otherwise its closure lies strictly between that component and a closed specialization, giving a chain of length two. Hence all points of $T$ are closed in $X$. Since $T$ is closed in $X$, an irreducible closed subset of $T$ is an irreducible closed subset of the scheme $X$ and so has a generic point; that point is closed, so the subset is a single point. Thus $\dim T\leq0$. The closed subscheme $T$ is Noetherian: locally its rings are quotients of Noetherian rings and its underlying closed subset is quasi-compact. Empty $Y$ or empty $Z$ gives empty $T$ and is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0E38, first paragraph; identification of the complementary closure by Tag 056B.

proof.text: Fix a closed point $y\in Y$, also closed in $X$. If $X$ is smooth over $k$ at $y$, take a smooth affine neighbourhood. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local] its local ring at $y$ is regular, hence a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] only one component passes through $y$: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $y=\mathfrak p$, the components of $X$ through $y$ are the closures of the components $V(\mathfrak q)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ minimal, and these $\mathfrak q$ are exactly the minimal primes of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ under the prime correspondence of localization. Remove the other finitely many components from a neighbourhood of $y$. The union description in Step 1 then identifies $Y$ and $X$ on that neighbourhood, since the unique incident component belongs to $Y$. Consequently $Y$ is smooth at $y$ and $y\notin T$.

source.place: Tag 0E38, smooth-point case; Algebra Tags 00TT, 00NP and 00ES.

proof.text: Now suppose $X$ is not smooth at $y$. Write $A=\mathcal O_{X,y}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_y$, $F=\kappa(y)$ and identify $C=\widehat A$ with $F[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as in the hypothesis; $F/k$ is finite separable. The ring $A$ is Noetherian and has dimension one: on each component through the closed point $y$, its generic point strictly specializes to $y$, and no chain of length two exists. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat], $A\to C$ is faithfully flat and its map on spectra is surjective. The one-variable power-series rings are local domains of dimension one by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete]. Therefore the prime ideals of $C$ are exactly $(u)$, $(v)$ and $(u,v)$: a prime contains $u$ or $v$, and its image in the corresponding one-variable quotient is either zero or the maximal ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], the maximal ideal of $C$ is $\mathfrak mC$ and contracts to $\mathfrak m$. Every minimal prime of $A$ is strictly smaller than $\mathfrak m$ and has a prime above it, so it is the contraction of $(u)$ or $(v)$. Thus $A$ has at most two minimal primes and $X$ at most two components through $y$, using [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes].

source.place: Tag 0E38, two-branch argument, using the prescribed split completion in place of the geometric-branches comparison.

proof.text: If $Y$ contains all components through this nonsmooth $y$ (including the case of a single component), remove the finitely many components not passing through $y$. Step 1 shows that $Y$ and $X$ coincide on the resulting neighbourhood. Their local $k$-algebras, residue fields and completions at $y$ agree. Thus $y$ is a split node on $Y$ with residue field finite separable over $k$, and $y$ does not lie in $Z$. It remains to consider the case where two distinct components pass through $y$ and exactly one belongs to $Y$.

In this remaining case let $\mathfrak p_1,\mathfrak p_2$ be the two minimal primes of $A$, with the first corresponding to $Y$ and the second to $Z$. Both are nonzero, since a zero prime would be contained in the other. Each $A/\mathfrak p_i$ is a reduced local domain essentially of finite type over $k$, of dimension one: $\mathfrak p_i\subsetneq\mathfrak m$ is a chain of length one and no longer chain exists. The completion clause of [lem-trf-curve-normalization-completion] says that $\widehat{A/\mathfrak p_i}$ is reduced of dimension one. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] this ring is canonically $C/\mathfrak p_iC$. Hence $\mathfrak p_iC$ is radical and its quotient has dimension one. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], a radical ideal is the intersection of its containing primes. The three-prime list in Step 3 therefore leaves only $0,(u),(v)$ when the quotient has dimension one: the intersection of both axes is zero, as the unique expansion $c+uf(u)+vg(v)$ shows, and the maximal ideal alone gives dimension zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], $\mathfrak p_iC$ contracts to the nonzero ideal $\mathfrak p_i$, excluding $0$; the same contraction identity shows the two extended ideals differ. After exchanging $u,v$, they are $(v)$ and $(u)$, respectively. In particular the completed quotient maps to $Y$ and $Z$ are exactly the two axis projections, not merely abstract isomorphisms of their targets.

source.place: Tag 0E38, identification of the completed component maps; Varieties Tag 0C3V and Algebra Tags 00MA, 05CK supply the expanded justification.

proof.text: The reduced component description of Step 1 identifies the local ideals of $Y$ and $Z$ at this point with $\mathfrak p_1$ and $\mathfrak p_2$. Their sum defines the scheme-theoretic intersection. Step 5 gives $(\mathfrak p_1+\mathfrak p_2)C=(u,v)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $(u,v)=\mathfrak mC$ and the residue field is unchanged. Contracting these equal ideals with [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] gives $\mathfrak p_1+\mathfrak p_2=\mathfrak m$. Thus $\mathcal O_{T,y}=A/(\mathfrak p_1+\mathfrak p_2)=F$ with its original $k$-algebra structure. In particular this is a reduced intersection of length one over its residue field.

source.place: Tag 0E38, sum-of-ideals calculation for the boundary; Algebra Tags 05GI, 05GG, 05CK.

proof.text: The completion of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}=A/\mathfrak p_1$ is $F[[u]]$ by Step 5. This is a regular local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local] to the Noetherian local quotient $A/\mathfrak p_1$: it is regular. Take an affine neighbourhood of $y$ on $Y$, whose coordinate ring is finite type over $k$ since it is a closed subscheme of a finite-type affine neighbourhood on $X$. Its residue field is the same $F$ as that of $X$ at $y$, finite and separable algebraic over $k$. Hence $F/k$ is separable in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]: a transcendence basis of the algebraic extension $F/k$ is empty, and every subextension $K'/k$ is separable algebraic, so separably generated with the empty transcendence basis. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-separable-residue-smooth] applies and proves that $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth at $y$.

source.place: Tag 0E38, final paragraph; More on Algebra Tag 07NY and Algebra Tag 00TV.

proof.text: Every closed point of $Y$ has now been considered. Step 2 makes it smooth if its ambient point is smooth; Step 4 preserves the prescribed split node when all incident components belong to $Y$; Step 7 makes it smooth when only one of two incident components belongs to $Y$. This proves (1). Every point of $T$ is closed by Step 1. It cannot be in the smooth case of Step 2 or the all-components case of Step 4, so it is in the two-components case. It is therefore a nonsmooth point of $X$ with exactly the completed local ring required by the original hypothesis, proving (2)(b), and Step 7 proves (2)(c). Step 6 supplies its residue field and its reduced local intersection ring.

source.place: Tag 0E38, assembly of the local cases.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete] to the Noetherian zero-dimensional scheme $T$ from Step 1. It has finitely many points, and each singleton is open. An open singleton in a scheme is the spectrum of its local ring: choose an affine neighbourhood of its point inside that open singleton, which must be the entire singleton, and then every denominator outside its unique prime is a unit. Step 6 identifies this ring as $F=\kappa(y)$ with its given $k$-algebra structure. Thus $T$ is a finite disjoint union of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$, each $\kappa(y)/k$ finite separable, proving (2)(a), including the empty union.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (2)(a), together with Properties Tag 0AAX and quasi-compactness for finiteness.

Checks by step: Step 1, the component-union node and the reduced scheme-theoretic closure, with all points of T closed in X. Step 2, smooth gives regular gives domain, so a single component passes through y. Step 3, using faithful flatness and surjectivity on Spec, the primes of F[[u,v]]/(uv) are exactly (u), (v), (u,v), so at most two minimal primes. Steps 5-6, the completion of A/p_i is C/p_iC, reduced of dimension 1; radicality, contraction and (u)∩(v)=0 force p_1C=(v) and p_2C=(u), and p_1+p_2=m. Step 7, 07NY and 00TV. Step 9, 0AAX gives a finite discrete T made of copies of Spec F. Small cases checked: Y empty, Y=X, one axis of uv=0 over F, both axes kept, an irreducible nodal curve, and a nontrivial finite separable F/k. I accept all ten declared tool_uses.
